propositions.statement: Let n be natural, X=R^n with Euclidean Lebesgue measure, F,D:R→X→R, t0∈R, s a neighborhood of t0, and b:X→R. Suppose F(t,·) is almost everywhere strongly measurable for t sufficiently near t0, F(t0,·) is integrable, D(t0,·) is almost everywhere strongly measurable, b is integrable, and for almost every x and all t∈s both |D(t,x)|≤b(x) and HasDerivAt (r↦F(r,x)) D(t,x) t hold. Then D(t0,·) is integrable and HasDerivAt (t↦∫x F(t,x) dx) (∫x D(t0,x) dx) t0.
